content: Primary discovery now runs through ck find-files with defaults top=20 and min-score=0.25. Explicit --top and --min-score continue to override defaults; query refinement is handled through ck get-keyword-map plus rerun of find-files.
LowRankDictionary filtering remains part of active query-time ranking and keyword hint generation. Folder-level combined_tokens persistence is no longer part of the active file-first indexing path.

Query-term specificity weighting based on document frequency exists in SourceMapSearcher and shifts exact-match influence toward discriminative terms. This currently applies to the legacy folder-ranking path, not the active ck find-files command path.

Layered query processing (low-rank filtering, generic normalization, sparse-term lexical backoff, DF-aware weighting) is implemented in SourceMapSearcher for folder ranking. Active CLI discovery currently uses the file-first lexical path via ck find-files.

Support-aware term weighting and sparse-term resolution exist in SourceMapSearcher to reduce unstable boosts from singleton terms. This behavior belongs to the legacy folder-search stack rather than active file-first retrieval.

Second-pass concentration reranking is implemented in SourceMapSearcher to reduce broad scope spread and improve path cohesion for ambiguous queries. This logic is currently in the legacy folder-ranking path, not active find-files lexical retrieval.

Hook policy now uses file-first boundaries: when ck find-files is broad/ambiguous, guidance requires ck get-keyword-map plus refined find-files. Guard flows also discourage repeated expand-folder loops without refinement and keep examples tooling-agnostic with ck commands.

Keyword-map acts as a decision engine: role buckets (anchor/discriminator/workflow/noise) are derived from corpus evidence and used to compose refined find-files queries plus concrete next-step commands. Broad-retrieval recovery is driven by keyword-map suggestions and remains tooling-agnostic via plain ck command output.

Keyword intent classification now uses corpus evidence (document-frequency percentiles, query/match support, and scoped-hint rank) instead of lexical/provider mappings. Query composition remains tooling-agnostic and emits generic ck next-step suggestions so behavior is consistent across Claude, Codex, OpenCode, and Agents integrations.

Release version mismatch root cause remains: ck --version is driven by hardcoded Program.Version in src/ContextKing.Cli/Program.cs, so tags/releases do not change reported version unless the constant is bumped. Installer local-asset detection is script-path based to avoid accidental CWD-driven stale asset usage in piped installs.

Active retrieval favors small file-level result sets from ck find-files with explicit top/min-score controls to keep context focused. Query processing stays repository-agnostic and lexical, with conservative keyword-map-assisted refinement when initial retrieval is weak or noisy.

ck find-files is now the primary file-first retrieval flow and ranks files lexically using folder path, filename, type names, and extracted method names from the source-map index. This removes dependency on prior folder-scope hops for initial discovery while staying aligned with CK extraction outputs.

Hook and protocol alignment treats ck find-files as the default discovery boundary across guard and hint flows, with keyword-map-assisted refinement and expand-folder as fallback exploration tools. Grep/Glob guidance points to file-first retrieval before fallback scoping, and postsession strong-signal detection includes find-files to keep knowledge-capture prompting aligned across shell and PowerShell hook variants.

Find-files uses persisted per-file lexical metadata (path, type names, method names, counts, hashes) in the source-map SQLite index with incremental refresh through SourceMapBuilder. This shifts work to index refresh-time and keeps repeated file-first retrieval fast without per-query full-repo rescans.

Index builds now run a parallel parse-to-persist pipeline for changed files: language extractors gather type/method names, then file rows are upserted into SQLite and stale paths removed by hash-based freshness. Folder rows are cleared in file-first mode during normal builds.

Legacy .ck-index SQLite schemas may lack files.type_names/method_names; read-only query paths must auto-run EnsureSchema and retry to avoid runtime crashes in get-keyword-map/find-files. Added retry-on-missing-column/table in SourceMapIndex reads so existing repos self-heal without manual reindex.
